newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: ICI Pakistan bond issue proves popular.
newsitem.headline: ICI Pakistan bond issue proves popular.

text.p: Investors have snapped up ICI Pakistan's bond issue, with a coupon of 18.7 percent a year, sparking hope for a revival of Pakistan's corporate debt market, analysts said on Sunday.

A Karachi Stock Exchange official said ICI Pakistan's issue of 5,000-rupee ($134.91) Term Finance Certificates (TFCs) worth 250 million rupees had attracted subscriptions worth 374.81 million rupees from the general public.

ICI Pakistan, a subsidiary of Britain's Imperial Chemical Industries Plc, also placed TFCs worth 750 million rupees with 21 institutional investors, including banks, financial institutions and mutual funds, the official said.
The five-year ICI certificate promises 18.7 percent annual interest, to be paid twice a year, which researchers described as the highest return in the public TFC market.

Raza Mirza, head of research at securities house Khadim Ali Shah Bukhari and Co Ltd, said the ICI Pakistan issue, worth a total one billion rupees, was the biggest of the seven TFCs issued so far in the Pakistani market.
"Its coupon rate is 18.7 percent, which is the highest return in the public TFC market and probably one of the highest available in the fixed-income market currently," he said.

"Even the pre-IPO list suggests a healthy appetite on the part of financial institutions for the ICI issue," Mirza said. "The reasons are obvious: most financial institutions would love to have ICI debt at 18.7 percent on their books."
He said capital gains from the ICI Pakistan TFC would be tax-exempt since it was listed on the Karachi stock exchange.
The issue seems to have begun well in the secondary market.

"Quotes in the grey market suggest premiums of one rupee on every 100 rupees for the TFC," said analyst Naz Chohan. "The ICI TFC should provide the impetus needed to revive the corporate debt market."
Dealer Manocher Jamal of Taurus Securities Ltd said the 18.7 percent coupon had been the main reason for the oversubscription in Pakistan's depressed capital market.
"The subscription is very encouraging and Pakistanis have reposed big confidence in the high-yielding ICI TFC," he said.
In May, ICI Pakistan offered a 325-for-100 rights issue to shareholders registered on June 11. It also offered a 220 percent rights issue in 1995.

The TFC issue will help to finance ICI Pakistan's $450 million pure terephthalic acid (PTA) plant being built near Karachi with a capacity of 400,000 tonnes a year. Production is due to start in November 1997.

The plant is expected to save Pakistan $100 million a year in foreign exchange now spent on PTA imports. It is being built with 61.5 percent equity financing from ICI Pakistan's British-based parent. The rest is being raised within Pakistan.
ICI Pakistan plans to add a second PTA plant after the year 2000, but has not decided the capacity of the second unit.
ICI Pakistan's 10-rupee share closed unchanged at 16.75 rupees at the Karachi bourse on Thursday, ahead of the Friday-Saturday weekend.
